youtube.baslik: How many decibels can a single nerve fiber code? #shorts
youtube.aciklama: The dynamic range of a single auditory nerve fiber is usually only about 20 to 40 dB, while the ear can handle a range of about 120 dB. The gap is closed by high, medium and low spontaneous rate fibers with different thresholds coming into play in turn.
youtube.kapanis_metni: Follow AIHEAR Audiology Academy for more quick facts.

sahneler.metin: How many *decibels* can one fiber code?
cumleler: How many decibels can a single nerve fiber code?

sahneler.alt: High spontaneous for soft, _low spontaneous for loud_ sounds
cumleler: A single fiber's dynamic range is usually only twenty to forty decibels.
Yet the ear handles about one hundred twenty decibels.
High spontaneous rate fibers respond to very soft sounds and saturate quickly.
Low spontaneous rate fibers keep working at high levels without saturating.
Fibers with different thresholds take over in turn to cover the range.
